title: Odd Edge Colorings of Graphs with Odd Order
summary: An {\em odd subgraph} of a graph is a subgraph in which every vertex has odd degree. A graph $G$ is said to be {\em odd $k$-edge-colorable} if there exists an edge-coloring $E(G) \rightarrow \{1,2, \ldots, k\}$ such that each non-empty color class induces an odd subgraph of $G$. The {\em odd chromatic index} of $G$, denoted by $χ'_o(G)$, is the minimum $k$ for which $G$ is odd $k$-edge-colorable.
